seoTitle: Molde cruise port guide: Varden walk, Romsdal Museum prices
seoDescription: Molde cruise port 2026: ships dock 100 m from the centre. Walk 4.4 km up to Varden (407 m) in 1.5 hours; Romsdal Museum 180 kr; Hjertøya boat 50 kr.
quickAnswer: Ships dock at Storkaia or Moldegård, about 100 m from the town centre, and the main square is a five-minute walk. The Varden viewpoint (407 m) is a 1.5-hour walk up the signed Green Corridor trail or about 10 minutes by car, and the Romsdal Museum lies on the way. Start back down from Varden at least 2 hours before you must be on board.
intro: Molde is a small town on the Romsdalsfjord, known as the town of roses, and the cruise quay is in the centre. The reason to come is the view: from Varden, 407 m above the town, you look across the fjord to a panorama of 222 peaks. The rest of the day fits around it. The Romsdal Museum's open-air houses sit on the slope below Varden, the cathedral and the rose-planted town hall roof are a few minutes from the quay, and in summer a 10-minute boat crosses to Hjertøya and its fisheries museum. The Atlantic Road is about 45 minutes away by road, so it needs a tour or a hire car.
tenderNotes: Ships normally dock at Storkaia or Moldegård. Anchoring with tenders is possible, about 500 m from the tender pier, if the quays are occupied.

terminals.name: Storkaia
terminals.notes: The main cruise quay, 300 m long, with no ship-size limit. About 100 m from the town centre and a five-minute walk to the main square. No shuttle bus is needed or provided, and Cruise Norway lists no restrooms on the pier.

terminals.name: Moldegård
terminals.notes: Second cruise quay, 130 m long, also in the centre.

walkability.detail: The town centre starts about 100 m from the quay and the main square (Torget) is about five minutes away. The cathedral and town hall are close by. The Romsdal Museum is about 10 minutes' walk from the centre, on the slope above. Varden is a real hike: 4.4 km and about 1.5 hours up the Green Corridor trail on asphalt, gravel and path, starting at the corner of Scandic Hotel Alexandra and marked with blue symbols.

transportSections.time: 5 min to Torget; 10 min from the centre to the Romsdal Museum
transportSections.detail: Everything in town is walkable. Visit Northwest says the self-guided town walk from Torget past the cathedral, town hall and Romsdal Museum suits people with reduced mobility, except the optional climb to Varden.

4.4 km from the sea at Reknes, through Reknes Park, past Rekneshaugen viewpoint and the Romsdal Museum to Varden at 407 m. Follow the blue symbols from the corner of Scandic Hotel Alexandra; markers show the distance left. Graded easy to medium.

transportSections.cost: Price not published; contact the operator (+47 919 95 030)
transportSections.time: About 15 min each way, 20 min at the top
transportSections.detail: Leaves from the town centre, stops 20 minutes at Varden and drops you at the Romsdal Museum on the way back. From there it is about 10 minutes' walk to the centre, or you can stay on the bus.

transportSections.cost: No fixed fares; ask for the price before you set off
transportSections.detail: In summer you can drive to Varden in about 10 minutes. Useful for going up and walking down the trail.

transportSections.cost: 50 kr adult, 25 kr child, 100 kr family (2026)
transportSections.detail: Summer only. Leaves from Reknesmoloen at the west end of Storgata, near the guest harbour. Operated by SeaFun (971 16 060); check departure times on seafun.no before planning around it.

transportSections.cost: 50 kr adult single, 1 zone; 25 kr child 6–17 and over-67s; 20 kr surcharge for adults buying on board (2026)
transportSections.detail: Few cruise visitors need the town buses. Bus 420 to Åndalsnes leaves from the Molde traffic terminal, crosses on the Sølsnes–Åfarnes ferry (included in the ticket) and connects with Rauma Railway trains; tickets in the FRAM or Entur app, or by card on board.

returnTiming.rule: Leave Varden on foot at least 2 hours before you must be on board, or 75 minutes before if you are driven down. From the town centre, start back 30 minutes before you must be on board.
returnTiming.detail: The walk down from Varden takes about 45 minutes, plus time at the museum or a café on the way. The quay is only about 100 m from the centre, so once you are in town the return is quick.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you are late on Varden, call a taxi rather than walking down; the road takes about 10 minutes. Call the port agent number in your daily programme if you are delayed.

excursionAdvice: For Molde itself, skip the ship tour if you can walk: Varden, the Romsdal Museum and the cathedral are all reachable on foot from the quay. If you cannot manage the climb, a ship tour or the local minibus to Varden is worth it. The Atlantic Road, Trollstigen and the Rauma Railway are different: they need road transfers, ferries or fixed train times, and Trollstigen takes 7–8 hours from Molde. Book those through the ship so it waits for you if something runs late.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes docking at Storkaia at 08:00, a summer call (22 June to 31 August, when the museum opens daily) and a clear morning.

steps.what: Walk from the quay to the corner of Scandic Hotel Alexandra and pick up the blue-marked Green Corridor trail.
Walk up through Reknes Park and past Rekneshaugen to Varden (about 1.5 hours).
Varden viewpoint. Coffee at Vardestua if it is open.
Walk down the trail to the Romsdal Museum.
Romsdal Museum: the open-air houses and the exhibitions in Krona (about 1.5 hours).
Lunch in the Krona café, or walk 10 minutes down to the centre for a bakery lunch at Fole Godt.
Molde Cathedral and the town hall roof garden, then a stroll along the seafront.
Back to the quay, about 100 m from the centre.
Back on board, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Varden viewpoint
sights.why: 407 m above the town, with views over the fjord, its islands and a panorama of 222 peaks, most over 1,000 m.
sights.tip: Walk up the Green Corridor (4.4 km, about 1.5 hours) or take a taxi up and walk down. Vardestua at the top is open roughly May to October.

sights.name: Romsdal Museum (Romsdalsmuseet)
sights.why: Open-air folk museum founded in 1912 with old farm and town buildings, plus Krona, the main building with exhibitions, a café and a shop.
sights.cost: 180 kr adult, 145 kr senior/student, 75 kr age 12–18; under-12s free (2026)
sights.tip: Krona opens daily 11:00–16:00 from 22 June to 31 August and is closed on Mondays outside summer. The open-air houses open with guides from 22 June to 16 August, and hours usually change on cruise days, so check the museum's cruise page.

sights.name: Green Corridor and Reknes Park
sights.why: The signed trail from the shore at Reknes through Reknes Park and past the Chateauet villa, with a viewpoint at Rekneshaugen before the climb to Varden.
sights.tip: Even if you do not go to the top, the lower section and Rekneshaugen give a good view over the town.

sights.name: Molde Cathedral (Molde domkirke)
sights.why: Consecrated in 1957 as the third church on the site, with a 50 m freestanding bell tower and Axel Ender's altarpiece, rescued from the earlier church fire.
sights.cost: No entry fee listed by Visit Northwest
sights.tip: At Kirkebakken 2, a few minutes from the quay. Services may limit visits.

sights.name: Town hall roof garden
sights.why: In summer the roof of the town hall is planted with roses and other flowers, the clearest sign of why Molde calls itself the town of roses.
sights.tip: Combine with the cathedral; both are on the self-guided town walk from Torget.

sights.name: Hjertøya and the Fisheries Museum
sights.why: A small island about 10 minutes by boat from Molde, home to the Romsdal Museum's Fisheries Museum.
sights.cost: Boat 50 kr adult; guided museum tour 180 kr adult (2026)
sights.tip: Guided tours run 14 June to 16 August at weekends at 12:15 and 15:15 (daily during Moldejazz, 13–19 July). There is no electricity on the island, so bring exact cash or buy the tour ticket online.

sights.name: Atlantic Road (Atlanterhavsveien)
sights.why: The coastal road of bridges and skerries about 45 minutes from Molde, with a short walk at Eldhusøya.
sights.tip: Local guided bus tours leave from Molde (Hamnegata 10 or the town centre). Only for long calls; otherwise book through the ship.

commonMistakes.mistake: Treating Varden as a quick stroll.
commonMistakes.fix: It is 4.4 km and about 1.5 hours up. If time is short, take a taxi up (about 10 minutes) and walk down in about 45 minutes.

commonMistakes.mistake: Expecting the Romsdal Museum's open-air houses to be open every day.
commonMistakes.fix: They open with guides from 22 June to 16 August and on most cruise days. Check the museum's cruise page for your date.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to reach the Rauma Railway from Molde on your own.
commonMistakes.fix: The line starts in Åndalsnes, a bus and ferry ride away. On a Molde call, take a ship excursion if you want the train.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going to Hjertøya with only a card.
commonMistakes.fix: There is no electricity on the island, so the guide takes exact cash only. Buy the museum tour online in advance.

commonMistakes.mistake: Buying a FRAM bus ticket from the driver.
commonMistakes.fix: Adults pay a 20 kr surcharge on board. Use the FRAM or Entur app.

safety: Molde is a small, quiet town with low crime. The practical risks are on the hill: the trail to Varden mixes asphalt, gravel and path and can be slippery after rain, and the weather on the top changes faster than in town. Wear proper shoes and carry a layer. In an emergency call 112 (police), 113 (ambulance) or 110 (fire).
scams: Taxis with no agreed fare: there are no fixed fares to Varden or the Atlantic Road. Ask for the price before you set off.
Paying the on-board surcharge on FRAM buses: adults pay 20 kr more for a single bought on board. Use the FRAM or Entur app.
Booking Atlantic Road tours from unofficial sellers at the quay. Use the operators listed by Visit Northwest or your ship, so you know the return time is fixed.
accessibility: The quay is about 100 m from the flat town centre, and Visit Northwest describes the town walk past the cathedral, town hall and Romsdal Museum as suitable for people with reduced mobility. The climb to Varden is not; go by taxi or the local minibus, which drives to the top and stops at the Romsdal Museum on the way back. Cruise Norway lists no restrooms in the pier area. Hjertøya has no electricity and is reached by a small boat, so it is difficult for wheelchair users.
rainyDay: Krona, the Romsdal Museum's main building, has permanent and temporary exhibitions, a café and a shop. Molde Cathedral is close to the quay. Skip Varden in low cloud, since the panorama is the whole point. The open-air museum works in light rain but not in a downpour.
crowdTips: There is no daily cruise cap in Molde and no cruise passenger fee in 2026: the government has proposed an optional municipal cruise fee of 100 kr per passenger per day from 1 January 2027. The Varden trail and the viewpoint are busiest when ship tours arrive, so walk up straight after docking. On cruise days the Romsdal Museum usually opens its houses with guides, and hours can change, so check its cruise page. During Moldejazz (13–19 July 2026) the town is busy and the museum moves some activities to the old town street, Bygata.

faqs.q: Is Molde cruise port walkable to the town centre?
faqs.a: Yes. Storkaia is about 100 m from the centre and the main square is about five minutes on foot.
Usually not. Ships dock at Storkaia or Moldegård in the centre. Anchoring with tenders is possible if the quays are full.

faqs.q: How do I get to the Varden viewpoint from the cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk the signed Green Corridor trail (4.4 km, about 1.5 hours up, 45 minutes down), take a taxi (about 10 minutes by road), or join the local minibus tour from the centre.

faqs.q: How much is the Romsdal Museum in 2026?
faqs.a: 180 kr for adults, 145 kr for seniors and students, 75 kr for ages 12–18, and free for under-12s with an adult.

faqs.q: Can I see the Atlantic Road from Molde on a cruise day?
faqs.a: Yes, with a tour or a hire car. It is about 45 minutes' drive each way, and local guided tours take 3.5–4.5 hours.

faqs.q: Can I ride the Rauma Railway from Molde?
faqs.a: Not directly. The line runs from Åndalsnes to Dombås (1 hour 20 minutes end to end), and Åndalsnes is a bus and ferry ride from Molde. Book it as a ship excursion.

faqs.q: What can I do in Molde in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Walk up to Varden for the view, visit the Romsdal Museum on the way down, then see the cathedral and the town hall roof garden near the quay.

faqs.q: Is Molde safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes. Crime is low. Take care on the Varden trail in wet weather.
